rationale: Round 0 built and passed with no ICE, so weights can be shifted modestly toward stronger obfuscation without risking the working baseline. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because arithmetic substitution suits this program's compute-heavy, branch-light kernels (isqrt, cubic, rad2deg) with low runtime and correctness cost. FLA stays moderately aggressive to flatten main's dispatch-heavy structure, but its RuntimeCost is raised slightly since main contains the program's loops. BCF is held back (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost) because bogus control flow inflates a tiny 2.6 KB text section disproportionately and slows the hot integer loops for modest marginal security over SUB+FLA. SPLIT is encouraged nearly unconditionally as the cheapest diversifier. IBR and ICALL remain enabled at moderate strength to break static call/branch graph reconstruction, with CorrectnessRisk kept at 0.3 since indirect addressing of a small function set is well-trodden. IGV is kept enabled but mild: the program has few globals, so its contribution is limited and it should not compete with higher-value passes.
